support_text: The DNA-damaging effect of compound 6a was evaluated using the SOS/umu test as a preliminary genotoxicity assay. All controls were correct (IF<2 for negative and IF>2 for positive controls). Compound 6a precipitated in wells with the highest tested concentrations (1, 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125 mg/mL), which were excluded. Compound 6a was considered non-genotoxic as its induction factor was always lower than 2 at non-cytotoxic concentrations (survival >80%) with or without the S9 fraction. The SOS/umu test is used for screening; regulatory confirmation would require the standardized Ames test.

support_text: The study evaluated the ability of new metallic-insecticides to change genetic material of non-target organisms using chromosomal aberration and micronucleus tests in the Allium cepa test system and the Trad-MCN test in Tradescantia pallida. One component of the formula, 5-methyl-phenanthroline, was also analyzed according to the same parameters. In Allium cepa, the analysis of 5-methyl-phenanthroline revealed that it can be related with the positive results, since genotoxic effects were induced. None of the metallic-insecticides showed genotoxic activity in the Trad-MCN test.
